task.agent_directive: Investigate TSMC's AI-related revenue: High Performance Computing (HPC) platform revenue, its share of total revenue, and AI accelerator demand, with cited figures.
constraints: Cite a source for every financial figure you record.
Use the most recently reported fiscal periods.
Focus on TSMC's HPC / AI-related business.
success_criteria: Report HPC platform revenue or share for recent quarters
Explain the role of AI accelerator demand

tool_arguments.query: TSMC Q3 2026 HPC platform revenue share of total revenue AI accelerator demand

events.content: TSMC Q3 2026 HPC platform revenue share of total revenue AI accelerator demand

TSMC’s high-performance computing (HPC) platform represented **68% of Q3 2026 revenue**, after rising **22% sequentially**. [[1]] 

With total Q3 revenue of **US$46.72 billion**, that implies HPC revenue of approximately **US$31.77 billion** for the quarter. [[2]] 

Management attributed the AI outlook to structurally strong AI-accelerator demand, supplemented by emerging demand for **agentic-AI CPUs** and continued demand for **networking chips**; it said broader adoption of agentic AI and open-source models should increase demand for leading-edge silicon. [[1]] 

TSMC’s prior outlook called for its narrowly defined AI-accelerators revenue to compound at a **mid- to high-50% CAGR from 2024 through 2029**; at Q3, management said demand was “extremely robust,” saw no slowdown, and indicated growth could be higher than that range. [[1]] 

The implication is that HPC’s 68% mix is not solely AI accelerators—TSMC’s HPC platform is broader—but the company explicitly identifies accelerators as the core support for AI-related demand, with CPUs and networking providing incremental upside. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Q3 2026 Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ... — https://investor.tsmc.com/english/encrypt/files/encrypt_file/reports/2026-10/eba4fac72873bf546b669bd2b5d973df5c93215d/TSMC%203Q26%20Transcript.pdf
